decisions.quote: Our results are also generally consistent with that study in terms of children’s gaze behaviour during the familiarization phase and its relation to their performance at test. In both studies, successful processing of the modified noun phrase and identification of the target during the familiarization phase did not necessarily lead to successful verb learning – in the condition we have labelled “Modified-Unnecessary,” children showed the same pattern in He et al. ( Reference He, Kon and Arunachalam 2020 ) (condition labelled “Heavy-Unnecessary”). Our results do differ slightly from those of He et al. in the Modified-Necessary condition. While children in our study did not look at the target at above-chance levels during familiarization, English learners did in the previous study, although in both studies this condition showed the worst performance (least target looking).
decisions.reason: While the authors confirm the unmodified-subject advantage in verb learning at test, they explicitly contrast a tested primary indicator (familiarization eye gaze in the Modified-Necessary condition, which was at chance here versus above chance in He et al., 2020); under the codebook rules, a stated contrast on a tested finding alongside replicated effects codes as mixed.
